output.summary: The referenced LT Verdict run is VALID with COMPLETE coverage, but the deterministic policy verdict is NO_POLICY for both the reference and evaluation windows, meaning no PASS/FAIL was produced. The load (target) was constant at 20 requests/s and was dropped as a control (CONSTANT_CONTROL) in every correlation pair, so all correlations were computed without a load control. Two correlation candidates were selected for the evaluation window: resource-00 vs p95 response time (rho 0.9746 at lag 0, Holm-adjusted p 0.016) and resource-06 vs p95 response time (rho 0.3769 at lag 0, Holm-adjusted p 0.016); all 14 other pairs were BELOW_EFFECT / NOT_SELECTED. Uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED throughout, sensitivity is not estimated, clock alignment is not verified by the core, and anomalies_tested = 0. Advice below treats these candidates as associations only and does not change the NO_POLICY verdict.

hypotheses.observation: pair-00 reports raw and partial rho of 0.974643249098 at best_lag_ms 0 for resource-00 vs response_time_p95_ms in the evaluation window, and the headline selection chose it with Holm-adjusted p-value 0.016 (max p 0.001), producing finding correlation-candidate pair-00.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Utilization of whatever system resource resource-00 measures may rise in step with slower p95 response time, e.g., queueing or contention on that resource during the evaluation window; this is an association, not a proven cause, and it is not controlled for load because the target control was constant.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run a controlled load ramp (target varying across the window) and re-measure pair-00 with the target as a usable control; verify clock alignment first, then inspect the physical definition of resource-00 and correlate with host/cgroup counters during the same timestamps.

hypotheses.observation: pair-06 reports raw and partial rho of 0.376900299123 at best_lag_ms 0 for resource-06 vs response_time_p95_ms in the evaluation window, and the headline selection chose it with Holm-adjusted p-value 0.016 (max p 0.001), producing finding correlation-candidate pair-06.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: resource-06 may be a secondary contributor to p95 latency variation, or its moderate rho plus statistical selection may reflect a shared background driver rather than a direct causal resource; the mechanism is not established.
hypotheses.recommended_check: With verified clocks, disaggregate the evaluation window by sub-intervals and by load step, and test whether the pair-06 association persists when resource-00 is included as an additional control.

hypotheses.observation: The target (load) series is constant at 20 requests/s (min = max = 20, standard deviation 0 in both windows), and every correlation pair dropped it as a control with reason CONSTANT_CONTROL, leaving controls_used empty and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null; meanwhile all resource ratio series range roughly 0.30-0.70 within each window.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because load did not vary, the ratio metrics still fluctuating ~0.3-0.7 implies either genuine system dynamics or shared/co-tenant or background activity; any simultaneous movement with latency could be coincidental external noise rather than load-driven coupling.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect out-of-band telemetry on co-tenant processes, host-level counters, and deployment/host assignment for the service during the evaluation window; compare resource-00 and resource-06 movements against those external signals.

hypotheses.observation: Latency upper tail is very tight: overall p99 = 239 ms and max = 240 ms, reference window p99 = 239 ms and max = 239 ms, evaluation window p99 = 239 ms and max = 240 ms, while p50 is 198 ms overall (192 reference, 200 evaluation).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A hard upper bound near 240 ms could indicate a configured deadline, timeout, or saturation cap in the load path rather than natural service-time behavior; this is unproven but worth checking given the round number.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify whether 240 ms corresponds to a configured JMeter timeout, client or service deadline, or backend cap; inspect the raw latency distribution and per-request histogram rather than only quantiles.

hypotheses.observation: With constant load at 20 requests/s in both windows, median latency increased from 192 ms (reference) to 200 ms (evaluation), and resource-00 mean utilization rose from 0.466406 (reference) to 0.5126145 (evaluation).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A change in system resource conditions between the two windows may coincide with the modest latency increase, but this is a timing coincidence unless clocks are verified and confounders are controlled; it cannot by itself establish that resource-00 caused the slower p95.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Segment metrics at finer granularity across the window boundary, verify source-clock alignment, and check for deployment, tenant, or environment changes between the reference and evaluation windows.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment and time synchronization across the load generator, service, and resource metric pipeline before drawing causal or lead/lag conclusions from this data.
recommendations.rationale: The resource-binding evidence reports clock_alignment = not_verified_by_core, and all selected correlations are at best_lag_ms 0; without a verified clock relationship, temporal ordering and causality are unsupported.

recommendations.action: Re-run the experiment with a non-constant target (e.g., ramp up / steady / ramp down) so the load control is not dropped and sensitivity and partial correlations can be estimated.
recommendations.rationale: The target was constant at 20 requests/s and every pair was analyzed with controls_used empty due to CONSTANT_CONTROL, leaving sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null; without load variation the rho values are association-only and cannot be separated from background effects.

recommendations.action: Define and attach an explicit policy (e.g., thresholds for p95 latency, error rate, or resource utilization) and re-evaluate so the run can yield PASS/FAIL.
recommendations.rationale: Both window policy summaries and the run policy verdict are NO_POLICY; a missing policy is not a pass, so the current verdict carries no performance-requirement conclusion even though selected correlation candidates exist.

recommendations.action: Investigate the identity of resource-00 and resource-06 and collect host/cgroup-level counters and application logs timestamped to the evaluation window to test whether those resources can explain p95 latency coupling.
recommendations.rationale: The selected candidates are the only findings of the run, but the evidence labels them only as service system ratio series; without resource identity and external counters, the mechanism behind rho 0.9746 and 0.3769 remains unknown.

recommendations.action: Add anomaly/availability analysis on longer runs and explicitly check the latency upper-tail behavior near 240 ms.
recommendations.rationale: This run reports anomalies_tested = 0 and episodes_reported = 0, so the absence of reported episodes does not prove stability or spare capacity; and p99 = 239 ms being essentially equal to max 240 ms in both windows warrants checking for a hard cap, deadline, or saturation artifact.

caveats: The deterministic verdict is NO_POLICY for the run and for both the reference and evaluation windows; this advisory preserves that verdict and does not treat missing policy as a pass or a fail.

Clock alignment is not verified by the core (clock_alignment = not_verified_by_core), so lag-0 correlations and reference-vs-evaluation window shifts cannot support lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypotheses.

The load target was constant at 20 requests/s in both windows and was dropped as a control in every correlation pair (reason CONSTANT_CONTROL); partial rho equals raw rho and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps is null in all pairs.
Uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED for all correlation pairs and for the diagnostic summary; no confidence intervals or effect sizes beyond rho are provided.

Correlation headline selection used the mbb-lag-max-holm.v1 method with 16 family hypotheses, block lengths 10/20 cells, 999 bootstrap replicates, and alpha 0.05; selection is hypothesis-test based and is not causal evidence.
anomalies_tested = 0 and episodes_reported = 0; this does not demonstrate stability, spare capacity, low load, or absence of problems.
Resource series are labeled only by opaque series_id (resource-00..resource-15) with unit ratio and role system; the physical resource identity is not present in the evidence.

Correlation pairs were computed only for the evaluation window; there are no reference-window correlation pairs, so changes in correlation structure before/after the window boundary cannot be compared.

Resource summaries are interval means with no missing cells, but within-cell variance and raw request timestamps are not provided, so sub-window or single-sample behavior cannot be inspected from this evidence.
Run-to epoch (1767225960180) extends 180 ms past the evaluation-to epoch (1767225960000); this small tail is not material but the exact handling of samples in that tail is not documented.
